doc.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23

title: Alfred Laine with Durante and Arnold Loyacano on TV
summary: Mrs. Laine says son Alfred played with Durante in New York in 1917, and recalls Loyacano calling the station about La Rocca's claims.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: That's the same year that Alfred went to New York. He played. He was with Durante, my son. That's right. He was with Durante. Yes, sir. We got Durante's card. His wife, he never fails sending him a Christmas card every year. And when he died, he sent him a beautiful card. Jimmy Durante? Yes. Fact. Yes. In 17, Alfred Lane was with Durante in New York in the Alamo Cafe. So how could...

I know one night, he'd come on TV, in the Rocker, with a whole lot of stuff. Yeah. And lawyer Kenner called my daughter. And her and him called up the station. And they told him what a liar he was and all that they didn't tell him. He picked up all these things and walked off the station and never seen them no more.
And I'll give it to him. He give it to him in no... No. That was Arnold Leuco. Arnold Leuco, yeah.
Poor Nick LaRocca never played no funeral. He couldn't play a funeral.
He knows Arnold Leuco knows that the Rocker didn't.
He couldn't play a funeral. He didn't know. He knows it.
